misconfig_patterns: rest-server started without .htpasswd (--no-auth) serves the full repo API unauthenticated on :8000

HARD GATE — restic is fully client-side-encrypted: /snapshots/ returns only SHA-256 object IDs, /config is an encrypted blob, no path/hostname/tag metadata is exposed server-side. AI/ML content CANNOT be confirmed from the wire. In-scope confirmation is external/metadata-only: reverse-DNS/TLS cert CN/Shodan org resolves to an AI/ML operator, OR aimap fingerprints an adjacent MLflow/Ollama/vector DB on the same IP (restic :8000 is that stack's backup tier), OR public IaC/docker-compose ties the rest-server volume to a model/training/embedding dir. The encrypted snapshot list is NOT evidence of AI data.

Restraint: names and counts ONLY. Snapshot/index/data IDs and their count are the finding. GET on any /data/<id>, /snapshots/<id>, /index/<id>, /keys/<id>, or the /config BODY pulls an encrypted repo blob = exfiltration, forbidden. Any POST/PUT (object upload, repo init) or DELETE is a write/destroy primitive, forbidden. The slash-username directory-traversal CVE is a write/cross-tenant primitive — document applicability from the version banner, never fire it. Stop at HEAD /config + the array of IDs.

response_markers: Content-Type response header value application/vnd.x.restic.rest.v2 (or .v1) on a list/object response — restic-protocol-unique
HEAD /config -> 200 with a tiny body == an initialized restic repo present at that path
GET /snapshots/ -> JSON array of 64-hex-char strings (v1) or array of {"name":"<64hex>","size":N} (v2) — all object names exactly 32-byte SHA-256 hex
401 with WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="restic" when .htpasswd auth is enforced (negative marker: confirms platform but gated)
Prometheus /metrics with rest_server_* metric names when --prometheus set
active_probe.false_positive_check: Require the exact Content-Type token application/vnd.x.restic.rest.* — never match on http.title or bare port:8000 (8000 is a very noisy dev/admin port: Django runserver, Splunk Web, SonarQube, Portainer agent). rclone serve restic emits the SAME content type but a different binary — disambiguate via Server header (rclone vs rest-server / Go-http-server). A 200 on GET /snapshots/ alone is not proof: an empty/non-repo path returns []; require non-empty 64-hex IDs AND a 200 on HEAD /config. Reject HTML or any non-hex token (catch-all/honeypot guard). 401/403 = surface-open-access-not-exercised, not a finding.

deployment_tells: Content-Type application/vnd.x.restic.rest.v2 (or .v1) on list/object responses — restic-protocol-unique
HEAD /config returns 200 with a tiny body == initialized restic repo at that path
GET /snapshots/ returns a strict JSON array of 64-char SHA-256 hex IDs (v1) or {name,size} objects (v2)
pivot_paths: HEAD /config -> confirm a repo exists at the default path (200) without pulling any blob
GET /snapshots/ -> enumerate snapshot object COUNT and IDs only (names are the finding; count = how many restore points exist)
GET /index/ and GET /locks/ -> index count gauges repo size; a present lock = a backup job is live right now (operator-activity signal, read-only)
GET /keys/ -> count of key files = how many passphrases/master-key slots guard the repo (more keys = shared/multi-user repo)
If --private-repos is suspected, probe HEAD /<likely-username>/config for sibling repos by name only (never traverse with a slash-username — that is the CVE write primitive, off-limits)
Correlate :8000 restic with aimap fingerprints on the same IP to attribute the backup to an AI/ML stack — all read-only, no object bytes fetched
vulnerabilities: GHSA-43vp-fcqq-x2q8 / SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMRESTICRESTSERVER-2404178: directory traversal in rest-server < 0.11.0 — a username containing a slash (e.g. foo/config) under --private-repos escapes its repo dir to read/delete another user's config/objects; CVSS 6.5; fixed 0.11.0 by restricting usernames to [unicode/0-9/-./@]

rest-server 0.10.0 pre-CVE (wojas): URL-encoded slash bypass of --private-repos path restriction (e.g. /foo/../bar) let one authenticated user reach another repo's objects; superseded by the 0.11.0 username-validation hardening
